answer.answer:
From GOV.UK's Child Benefit guide (https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit):

HOW IT WORKS (https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-it-works): You get Child Benefit if you're responsible for bringing up a child who is under 16, or under 20 if they stay in approved education or training. Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child, and there's no limit to how many children you can claim for. By claiming you can get: an allowance paid for each child (usually every 4 weeks); National Insurance credits that count towards your State Pension; and a National Insurance number for your child. You'll get NI credits automatically if you claim and your child is under 12. You must report any change of circumstances to the Child Benefit Office.

ELIGIBILITY / WHO CAN GET IT (https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility): Only one person can get Child Benefit per child. You normally qualify if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. You're usually responsible if you live with them, or you pay at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent in kind) towards looking after them. If your child is 16 or over, you'll normally still qualify if they're under 20 and stay in approved education or training; you can apply to continue for 20 weeks if a 16/17-year-old leaves education/training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Rules cover fostering (qualify unless the council pays towards accommodation/maintenance), adopting (can claim as soon as the child lives with you), looking after someone else's child, and living abroad. If you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme you can claim; with pre-settled status there are conditions (working above the primary threshold for 3 continuous months, jobseeker for 91 days, sufficient resources, studying, etc.). You'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts paid work 24+ hours a week and is no longer in approved education/training, starts an apprenticeship in England, or starts getting certain benefits.

HOW TO CLAIM (https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim): You can claim 48 hours after registering the birth, or once a child comes to live with you. Claims can be backdated up to 3 months from the claim date. Only one person can claim per child, and you should decide who claims (the claimant gets NI credits). Before starting you'll need: your child's birth/adoption certificate (if you have it), your bank/building society details, your National Insurance number (if you have one), and your partner's NI number (if you have a partner). You can claim online via the 'Start now' service of HMRC, or by post or phone if you cannot apply online. If you don't have the birth/adoption certificate you can still claim (it takes longer). I stopped before the online claim service, which would require signing in and entering personal data.

HOW IT WORKS (https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit): You get Child Benefit if you're responsible for bringing up a child who is under 16, or under 20 if they stay in approved education or training. Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child, and there's no limit to how many children you can claim for. By claiming you can get: an allowance paid for each child (usually every 4 weeks), National Insurance credits which count towards your State Pension, and a National Insurance number for your child without them applying. You'll get National Insurance credits automatically if you claim and your child is under 12; these count towards your State Pension if you're not working or don't earn enough to pay NI contributions. If you don't need the credits, your husband/wife/partner can apply to transfer them, or a different family member providing care can apply for Specified Adult Childcare credits. You must report any change of circumstances to the Child Benefit Office.

ELIGIBILITY / WHO CAN GET CHILD BENEFIT (https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility): You normally qualify if you're responsible for a child under 16 and live in the UK. You're usually responsible if you live with them, or you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent in kind) towards looking after them (e.g. food, clothes, pocket money). If your child is 16 or over, you normally still qualify if they're under 20 and stay in approved education or training; you can apply to continue for 20 weeks if a 16/17-year-old leaves education/training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Fostering: you get it if you foster a child, as long as the local council isn't paying anything towards their accommodation or maintenance. Adopting: you can claim as soon as the child comes to live with you. Looking after someone else's child: possible under an informal arrangement to look after a friend/relative's child, but you might not qualify if the council pays towards accommodation/maintenance. Two people cannot get Child Benefit for the same child - agree who claims, or HMRC decides; you may also be entitled to Guardian's Allowance. Living abroad / EU Settlement Scheme: you may get it if you move to certain countries or are a Crown servant; with settled status you can claim; with pre-settled status you can claim if working (earning above the primary threshold for 3 continuous months), jobseeking (up to 91 days), have sufficient resources, studying (must have sufficient resources), or are a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with a right to reside. You'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts paid work 24+ hours a week and is no longer in approved education/training, starts an apprenticeship in England, or starts getting certain benefits in their own right.

HOW TO CLAIM / MAKE A CLAIM (https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim): You can claim 48 hours after registering the birth, or once a child comes to live with you; it can be backdated up to 3 months. Only one person can claim per child - decide who, since whoever claims gets National Insurance credits towards their State Pension. You and your partner can claim for different children, but if living together only one can claim the higher rate (for the eldest child). If under 16, either claim for your own child or have someone responsible claim on your behalf. Make a claim online (or by post/phone if you cannot apply online). Before you start you'll need: your child's birth or adoption certificate (if you have it), your bank/building society details, your National Insurance number (if you have one), and your partner's National Insurance number (if you have a partner). Claims for children born outside the UK need the original birth/adoption certificate plus the child's passport or travel document. answer.answer:
From GOV.UK Child Benefit guide (https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit):

HOW IT WORKS: You get Child Benefit if you're responsible for bringing up a child who is either under 16, or under 20 if they stay in approved education or training. Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child, and there's no limit to how many children you can claim for. By claiming you get an allowance paid for each child (usually every 4 weeks), National Insurance credits which count towards your State Pension, and a National Insurance number for your child (usually shortly before they turn 16). If you choose not to get the payments, you should still make a claim to get the other advantages. You get National Insurance credits automatically if you claim and your child is under 12; these fill gaps if you're not working or don't earn enough to pay NI. You must report any change of circumstances to the Child Benefit Office.

ELIGIBILITY (Who can get Child Benefit): Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. You normally qualify if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. You're usually responsible if you live with them, or you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent in kind) towards looking after them (e.g. food, clothes, pocket money). If your child is 16 or over, you normally still qualify if they're under 20 and stay in approved education or training; you can apply to continue for 20 weeks if a 16/17-year-old leaves education/training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Fostering: you get it if you foster, as long as the local council isn't paying towards accommodation/maintenance. Adopting: you can claim as soon as the child comes to live with you (no need to wait for completion). Looking after someone else's child: possible with an informal arrangement, but may not qualify if the council pays towards their accommodation/maintenance. Two people cannot get it for the same child - if you can't agree, HMRC decides. Different rules apply for children in hospital/care or living with someone else, for living abroad, for EU Settlement Scheme status (settled or pre-settled), and you'll stop getting it if your child starts paid work 24+ hours/week and is no longer in approved education/training, starts an apprenticeship in England, or starts getting certain benefits.

HOW TO CLAIM (Make a claim): You can claim 48 hours after registering the birth, or once a child comes to live with you; it can be backdated up to 3 months from the claim date. Only one person can claim per child - decide who should claim, since the claimant gets the National Insurance credits towards their state pension. You and your partner can claim for different children, but if you live together only one of you can claim at the higher rate for the eldest child. If you're under 16 you can claim for your own child or someone responsible for you can claim on your behalf. You can make a claim online (or by post/phone if you cannot apply online). Before you start you'll need: your child's birth or adoption certificate (if you have it), your bank/building society details, your National Insurance number (if you have one), and your partner's National Insurance number (if you have a partner). You can still claim without the certificate - it will take longer and you may be asked to send it. If the birth was registered outside the UK you'll need the original certificate plus the child's passport/travel document (eVisa details are checked automatically, no share code needed). Note: this only involved reading public pages - no sign-in, account, payment, or personal data was entered.

answer.answer:
From GOV.UK's Child Benefit guide (https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit), reading the 'How it works', 'Who can get Child Benefit' (eligibility) and 'Make a claim' sections. I did not sign in, create an account, or enter any personal data, and stopped before the online 'Start now' claim service.

HOW IT WORKS: You get Child Benefit if you're responsible for bringing up a child who is under 16, or under 20 if they stay in approved education or training. Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child, and there's no limit to how many children you can claim for. By claiming you get: an allowance paid for each child (usually every 4 weeks), National Insurance credits that count towards your State Pension, and a National Insurance number for your child without them having to apply (usually shortly before they turn 16). If you choose not to get the payments, you should still make a claim to get the other advantages. Child Benefit and protecting your State Pension: you get NI credits automatically if you claim and your child is under 12, which prevents gaps in your NI record if you're not working or don't earn enough to pay NI contributions; if you don't need the credits your husband/wife/civil partner can apply to transfer them, or another family member who cares for your child can apply for Specified Adult Childcare credits. You must report any change of circumstances to the Child Benefit Office.

ELIGIBILITY (Who can get Child Benefit): Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. You normally qualify if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. You'll usually be responsible if you either live with them, or you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them - for example on food, clothes or pocket money. Eligibility rules are different if your child goes into hospital or care, or lives with someone else.

HOW TO CLAIM (Make a claim): You can claim Child Benefit 48 hours after you've registered the birth of your child, or once a child comes to live with you, and claims can be backdated up to 3 months from the date you make the claim. Only one person can claim for a child, so decide who should claim (whoever claims gets the National Insurance credits towards their State Pension). You and your partner can claim for different children, but if you live together only one of you can claim at the higher rate for the eldest child in the household. If you're under 16 you can claim for your own child, or someone responsible for you can claim on your behalf. Before you start you'll need: your child's birth or adoption certificate (if you have it), your bank or building society details, your National Insurance number (if you have one), and your partner's National Insurance number (if you have a partner). Without a certificate you can still claim but it takes longer; if the birth was registered outside the UK you'll need to send the original birth/adoption certificate and the child's passport or travel document used to enter the UK (eVisas are checked automatically, no share code needed). If you cannot apply online you can claim by post or by phone, and you may be able to manage someone else's Child Benefit claim.
